newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BNZ embarking on restructuring exercise.
newsitem.headline: BNZ embarking on restructuring exercise.

text.p: The Bank of New Zealand is undergoing a restructuring exercise involving around 200 staff but the final number of redundancies is unknown, spokesman Rowan McArthur said on Friday.
"There are in the vicinity of 200 roles being reassessed or reassigned where people have to reapply for jobs," he said.
"Alot of those will be successful and some of them won't."
The proocess would not be finished for six to eight weeks.
"It won't be until then that we will know how many redundancies are involved," McArthur said.

Wellington Regional Secretary of the bank workers' union, FinSec, Blair O'Brien, said he was aware of a BNZ restructuring of management positions where many managers had received letters saying their job was surplus.
"There are likely to be redundancies for BNZ managers but that is down the track," he said.
He said the banking industry was in an almost continuous state of restructuring.
McArthur said the National Australia Bank owned BNZ would not be making any announcement about layoffs and total net staff levels would remain about the same as at present.

"What we are embarked on at the moment, as most large organisations are in the financial services sector, is a reorganisation, reshaping, refocus, or restructuring of the organisation, particularly at the network end.
"It's an exercise driven by the need to reshape the branch network as opposed to cutting staff numbers to meet some sort of cost-income requirement."
The restructuring has been prompted by the changing nature of how the bank delivers its services, particularly the influence of automated technology.

Branches with little foot traffic were being closed. Many customers were spending less time in the banks as they increasingly use EFTPOS machines and that was putting pressure on branches with relatively fewer customers, particularly in rural areas.
BNZ is attempting to get customers affected by branch closures onto automated services.
O'Brien said further redundancies in the industry were expected in WestpacTrust following the takeover by Westpac of Trust Bank. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
